subject: Intermittent streaming slowpath observed — ops bridge notes & temporary mitigations
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@orbitai.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:02:00Z
Subject: Intermittent streaming slowpath observed — ops bridge notes & temporary mitigations

Hi Rajiv —

Thank you again for the quick call this morning. We saw the elevated per-token latency on your live-chat websocket connections between ~08:45–09:15 UTC affecting a small subset of sessions in us-east-1. We ran an ops bridge with infra and serving and wanted to capture exactly what happened and the short-term steps we took so you have a single place to reference.

Summary (high-level):
- Impact: sporadic token emission delays for streaming/chat (clients experienced pauses of 600ms–2s on some connections). No dropped messages or misordering observed.
- Root cause (initial): elevated KV-cache churn on a subset of host shards due to an uncharacteristic request distribution combined with our recent strict prefix-eviction heuristic.

Immediate mitigations applied (what we did):
1) Temporarily disabled the strict prefix-eviction heuristic on the affected shard pool to reduce KV cache thrash (rolled at 09:00 UTC).
2) Enabled a short-term model-variant fallback rule in routing that sends heavy-streaming sessions to a lower-memory variant (same semantics, smaller KV footprint).
3) Adjusted streaming ACK window on the proxy from 64k->32k bytes to reduce head-of-line stalls for long-lived websockets.
4) Restarted the three affected inference nodes sequentially to clear pathological cache state.

Client-side recommendations (what you can do now):
- Reduce your client chunk size to 512–1024 bytes for 30 minutes while we validate steady-state.
- If you see repeated 1.5s+ stalls, please toggle connection keepalive at 20s and re-open the socket — this helps session routing to a fresh host.
- If you can, enable our 'allow-fallback' routing header (x-rw-allow-fallback: true) so we can transparently route to the smaller model variant without a change on your side.

Attachments: we've attached extracted traces and the ops-bridge notes (stream-trace-20261115.json, ops-bridge-notes-20261115.pdf).

Next steps (we own):
- Postmortem with timeline and permanent remediation by EOD Friday.
- We'll validate telemetry to ensure no regressions over the next 48 hours.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute post-incident walkthrough next week.

Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming latency affects critical UX. Happy to jump on a call if you'd like more color.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

The ops bridge timeline points to cache eviction policy interacting badly with a skewed session distribution. We're including the trace so your SRE can review correlation.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T16:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: timeline & next steps (draft)

Team —

This is the draft post-incident update we will share with OrbitAI after Monday's validation window. Posting here so Monica can forward and Rajiv has the public timeline. Please review for technical correctness.

Draft timeline (short):
- 08:43 UTC: First elevated token latency alert from telemetry for orbitai-prod (streaming token p50->p95 jump).
- 08:48 UTC: Ops bridge opened; on-call assigned (rishi).
- 08:52 UTC: Confirmed impact on 3 host shards, KV-cache eviction rates 8x baseline.
- 09:00 UTC: Disabled strict prefix-eviction heuristic on affected shard pool (rollbackable).
- 09:03 UTC: Enabled model-variant fallback for heavy-streaming sessions.
- 09:06–09:12 UTC: Sequential rolling restart of affected nodes; observed latency normalize by ~09:14 UTC.

Root cause analysis (short):
- Contributing factor A: recent change to the prefix-eviction heuristic interacted with skewed session locality, causing excessive KV cache churn.
- Contributing factor B: a small proportion of long-lived streaming sessions generated long contiguous KV growth patterns that amplified eviction pressure.

Remediations (planned):
- Short (1–3 days): Keep fallback routing enabled for OrbitAI (72h TTL); monitor KV churn metrics and adjust eviction threshold.
- Medium (1–2 weeks): Introduce a soft cap on per-session KV growth and add a per-host eviction backlog metric to alert earlier.
- Long (3–6 weeks): Rework prefix-eviction to be workload-aware and add a canary for new eviction heuristics.

Client asks for OrbitAI:
- Continue with the client chunk-size reduction (512–1024 bytes) during the 72h window.
- Enable x-rw-allow-fallback: true so we can route gracefully if a host is under memory pressure.

Credits/comp: Monica to propose a small usage credit for the impacted window; I'll include suggested wording on Friday.

Please comment by EOD tomorrow; otherwise we'll send the customer-facing postmortem on Monday.

Thanks — Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Production Engineer, Redwood Inference
